Eyeball Grabber Wanted: You’ve written ads that interrupted the scroll. Emails that earned the click. Landing pages that made the offer feel obvious. Video scripts that hooked fast and held attention. And sales copy that turned complicated product benefits into simple, human, persuasive messages. You know how to write with empathy, clarity, proof, and punch. You can take a clinical study, a customer insight, a product USP, or a messy brief and turn it into copy that feels easy to read and hard to ignore.
 If that sounds like you, here’s your next big opportunity:
 We want a Copywriter to help us write high-performing, conversion-focused copy across ads, emails, sales pages, social, video scripts, blogs, and more.
 Small print here ⇒ We’re a women’s health supplement company. So if you can’t write in a way that makes women feel heard, understood, and safe enough to trust you… this isn’t the role for you. 
 Still here? Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels:
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your words will help more women discover those solutions.
 Your copy will help a menopausal woman understand her body better. Feel more confident in her choices. Take action. And maybe even change the way she thinks about her health, her future, and what’s possible for her.
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your copywriting career than here.
 This job might be for you if you’ve got…
 3–5 years of proven copywriting experience. When we look at your portfolio we’ll see a full-spectrum of ads, emails, landing pages, and sales pages that converted like a Kentucky Tent Revival. There’s no doubt about it… your copy SELLS!    
 Direct response chops that make your words cut through the clutter. You know how to write hooks, leads, headlines, subject lines, bullets, offers, calls-to-action, and sales arguments that pull people in and keep them reading. If you can make a reader think, “Okay, I need to know where this is going,” we want to talk.
 A Makepeace-like ability to turn product features into customer benefits. You don’t stop at “contains calcium, magnesium, boron, and vitamin D3.” You ask: Why does that matter? What does the customer already believe? What are they afraid of? What have they tried? What do they need to understand before this feels worth buying?
 A brain that can find the story in the science. You dig through a database of clinical studies, spot the strongest marketing nuggets, and turn them into a compelling product story. You don’t just summarize research. You connect the ingredients, doses, mechanisms, and results in a way that is clear, accurate, persuasive, and easy for a real human to understand. Bonus points if you’ve done this in health, wellness, supplements, or women’s health.
 A performance-driven approach to writing. You don’t treat copy like precious art carved into marble. You want to know what worked, what didn’t, and what to test next. CTR, CVR, CPA, open rate, click rate, rankings, traffic, revenue — these numbers don’t bruise your ego. They sharpen your instincts.
 A full-funnel writing brain. You understand that a Meta ad, an email, a sales page, a video script, an organic post, and a blog all have different jobs. You can shift tone, format, pace, and depth depending on the channel, while keeping the message consistent and on-brand.
 A strong understanding of hooks, angles, and offers. You know the difference between a headline that states a fact and a hook that creates momentum. You can find fresh angles in customer reviews, testimonials, research papers, competitor funnels, product details, and the quiet little objections most writers miss.
 The ability to write both short and long. You can write a 12-word ad hook, a 90-character description, a PWAT-style email, a 6,000-word sales page, or a VSL-style script without losing the thread. You know when to be punchy, when to explain, when to agitate, and when to get out of the reader’s way.
 A thick portfolio that shows you can sell. Show us copy that made people click, buy, book, watch, download, subscribe, or take the next step. And if you have results, bring them. We love results around here. We may even clap.
 A detective’s eye for customer insight. Reviews. Surveys. Testimonials. Comments. Competitor pages. Sales calls. Clinical studies. You know the best copy rarely starts with a blank page. It starts with listening.
 Experience writing SEO, AEO, or GEO content. You can write helpful, searchable content without sounding like you swallowed a keyword spreadsheet. You know how to answer real questions clearly, structure information well, and still make the copy feel warm, useful, and human.
 A healthy respect for compliance, claims, and accuracy. We work in the health space, which means “sounds convincing” is not good enough. Your copy needs to be truthful, sourced, compliant, and trustworthy. You know how to make a strong point without wandering into forbidden-claim territory wearing a blindfold.
 A detail-oriented editing brain. You catch typos, clunky transitions, unsupported claims, awkward phrasing, missing context, and sentences that sound like they were written by a robot with a vitamin deficiency.
 The ability to use AI without letting AI use you. You’re comfortable using AI tools for research, ideation, outlining, variation, and speed. But you still bring the strategy, taste, judgment, empathy, and final polish. 
 A collaborative, receptive attitude. You’ll work with marketers, designers, video editors, stakeholders, and other writers. You’ll get feedback. Sometimes a lot of it. You don’t need to defend every sentence like it’s a beloved family heirloom. You listen, revise, improve, and make the work better.
 The organization to handle multiple projects without going feral. Ads, emails, blogs, scripts, landing pages, revisions, research, feedback, deadlines — you can keep things moving, communicate early, and let people know when something is blocked.
 A genuine curiosity about the customer. You want to know what she’s worried about. What she’s tried. What she believes. What she secretly fears. What would make her feel relieved. What would make her trust us. That curiosity is what makes your copy feel like it was written for a person, not an avatar on someone’s Canva slide.
 Ecommerce experience would be lovely. Supplement experience would be even lovelier. Women’s health experience might make us swoon. But the real must-haves are strong direct response fundamentals, excellent research ability, clean writing, emotional intelligence, and a hunger to get better.
 Now, time to be honest: is this really you?
 If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you.
 But if you think copywriting is mostly “story telling” or “making things sound nice,” this probably isn’t the role for you.
 We need someone who can write with heart and strategy.
 Someone who can make complex health information feel simple.
 Someone who can take feedback without crying like a baby.
 Someone who can care about the customer and the conversion.
 Someone who can write a subject line in the morning, research a clinical study before lunch, polish a landing page in the afternoon, and still have the brainpower to ask, “Is this actually the strongest angle?”
 If that sounds like you, you may have just found your people.
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own.
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve your craft, and keep getting sharper.
 You’re people smart — in the sense that you’re a thoughtful, communicative, generous teammate.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at AlgaeCal.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that is a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better.
 Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skill, curiosity, work ethic, and copywriting talent, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches if you work from our Vancouver office
 Incredible dog-friendly Yaletown office one block from SkyTrain
 Remote working is okay with us too
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun, support each other, and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of Team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer our successful applicant.
 So, to make sure our future Copywriter is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive at AlgaeCal, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume, cover letter, and writing sample.
 Please read carefully:
 Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Copywriter for this role? Give quantifiable examples of related achievements.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What's the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 Explain what you’re doing now for a job:
 If you don’t have one, explain why.
 If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure that your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Must attach a piece of copy you’ve written.
 We want to see a sales page or landing page that you’ve written that clearly demonstrates your understanding of direct response marketing.  
 Please include the results it produced, if available. We love seeing real-world performance.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best — and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter, resume, and writing sample. 
 Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read! 
 We are looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly and you can expect a prompt response.

The objective of this assignment is to ensure the successful production and delivery of high-quality Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBAs) from a strategic supplier. The selected consultant will work onsite at the supplier's manufacturing facility to monitor production activities, oversee quality compliance, identify manufacturing risks, and coordinate with supplier and customer stakeholders to ensure products are delivered on time and meet all technical and quality requirements.
 Key Responsibilities
 Production Surveillance 
 Monitor production planning and execution against agreed schedules and priorities.
 Track manufacturing progress and identify production constraints, material shortages, and capacity risks.
 Follow up on recovery plans and ensure timely implementation of corrective actions.
 Escalate issues that could impact production schedules or customer deliveries.
 Quality Surveillance 
 Monitor incoming, in-process, and final inspection activities.
 Verify compliance with engineering drawings, specifications, approved manufacturing processes, and quality standards.
 Ensure effective management of non-conforming products, rework activities, and corrective actions.
 Monitor containment actions and verify implementation of permanent corrective actions.
 Supplier Performance Management 
 Conduct regular operational reviews with supplier management.
 Monitor supplier production, delivery, and quality performance.
 Identify operational risks and drive mitigation plans.
 Coordinate with Supply Chain, Engineering, Manufacturing, and Quality teams to resolve technical and operational issues.
 Reporting & Communication 
 Prepare weekly status reports covering production progress, delivery performance, quality concerns, risks, and action plans.
 Maintain an open action tracker and quality issue log.
 Immediately communicate any issue that could impact product quality, production continuity, or delivery commitments.
 Provide recommendations to improve supplier manufacturing performance and establish sustainable process control.
 Required Qualifications 
 Minimum 5 years of experience in PCB/PCBA manufacturing, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related electronics manufacturing environment.
 Strong understanding of PCB/PCBA manufacturing processes and electronics production.
 Experience in supplier development, supplier quality engineering, manufacturing surveillance, or industrial performance improvement.
 Working knowledge of IPC standards and AS9100 and/or ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems .
 Experience using structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, 5 Why Analysis, Root Cause Analysis (RCA), Fishbone, etc. 
 Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
 Ability to work independently at the supplier's manufacturing facility while effectively collaborating with supplier leadership and customer teams.
 Deliverables
 The consultant will be expected to provide:
 Weekly production and quality status reports.
 Open action tracker.
 Risk assessment and recovery plan follow-up.
 Quality issue log.
 Recommendations for continuous improvement of supplier manufacturing and quality performance.
 Success Criteria
 The engagement will be considered successful based on:
 Stable production execution aligned with agreed schedules.
 On-time delivery of required quantities.
 Delivery of PCBAs meeting all technical, manufacturing, and quality requirements.
 Effective management and timely closure of production and quality issues.
 Sustainable improvements in supplier manufacturing performance and process control.
 If you have qualified candidates with relevant PCB/PCBA manufacturing and supplier quality experience who are available to start immediately, please share their updated resumes along with the following details:
 Total Experience
 Relevant PCB/PCBA Manufacturing Experience
 Supplier Quality/Manufacturing Surveillance Experience
 Experience with IPC, AS9100, and/or ISO 9001
 We would appreciate receiving suitable profiles at the earliest due to the urgent nature of this requirement.

The role spans front-of-house reception, facilities and supplies, shipping, and health and safety, alongside the events, team lunches, and swag that bring the office together. It will suit someone who takes pride in a well-run workplace and enjoys creating the moments that bring a team together.



This role is expected to leverage AI and emerging technologies to improve productivity, enhance decision-making, and continuously optimize how work is performed.



This will be a full-time, permanent position working out of the Vancouver office, on-site five days per week.



What You'll Be Doing:

 - Own the front-of-house experience — welcome visitors, candidates, and vendors, answer and route incoming calls, correspondence, and the shared office inbox within agreed response times, and keep the office secure by maintaining the visitor log and issuing badges.

 - Keep the office running day to day through regular walkthroughs, meeting room checks, upkeep across multiple kitchens, and daily supply ordering and inventory, receipt reconciliation, liaising with building maintenance and janitorial staff to resolve issues quickly.

 - Coordinate vendors and manage swag orders for employee onboarding and one- and five-year anniversaries, including custom LEGO swag and Trulioo Values bricks. Manage the shipment of equipment, swag, and other items through FedEx, DHL, and other courier services.

 - Curate the in-office experience alongside the Workplace Experience Lead — monthly events spanning ERG, wellness, cultural, social, and DE&I programming, twice-weekly team lunches, from researching restaurants across the city to placing the order, and a monthly happy hour.

 - Chair the Health and Safety Committee, running the monthly meeting and keeping the office's safety practices, training, and documentation current.

 - Keep recurring office administration on schedule — onboarding and offboarding tracking, monthly budget and invoice reporting for office purchases, anniversary date reports, and the monthly reporting that supports our internal compliance requirements.

 - Leverage AI and emerging technologies to improve productivity, streamline workflows, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement while ensuring the responsible, secure, and compliant use of AI tools.

 - Use AI assistants to triage and summarize the shared office inbox, draft event and office communications, and pull together recurring monthly reports from existing data.
   
   

What You'll Bring:

 - Education: Bachelors of Business Administration or equivalent experience. CPR-C and AED certification, or willingness to become certified through Trulioo.

 - Experience: 2–4 years in Hospitality or Facilities field, office coordination, reception, or administrative support.

 - Soft skills: Warm, professional communication with everyone from candidates to executives; a calm, organized approach to competing priorities; and the flexibility to change direction when the day does.

 - Hard skills: Inventory and supply management, vendor coordination, invoice and budget tracking, courier and shipping logistics, event planning, and recurring monthly reporting. Able to be on your feet for long periods and lift 50lbs.

 - Technology: Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets), Slack, Zoom, Navan and courier portals such as FedEx and DHL.
   
   

Nice to Have:

 - AI fluency: Comfort using AI assistants such as Claude or Gemini to draft, summarize, and organize daily work, with the judgment to review output before it goes out and to handle confidential information appropriately.

 - Facilities or building operations experience:  coordinating with property management on maintenance, repairs, and building access, and holding on-site vendors to their service standards.

 - A hospitality, concierge, or events background, and the service standard that comes with it.

 - Working knowledge of Vancouver's restaurant and venue scene for lunches, socials, and offsites.

 À La Caisse :
 On valorise votre apport unique au sein d’une équipe d’envergure mondiale.
 On vous confie un travail qui vous permet de vous épanouir et de vous dépasser.

 Description d'emploi 
 L’équipe de Gouvernance financière veille à la fiabilité de l’information financière en assurant la surveillance des contrôles internes à l’égard de l’information financière (CIIF) et des contrôles et procédures de communication de l’information (CPCI), dans le cadre du programme d’attestation financière.  Ce que vous ferez 
 Gouvernance et surveillance des contrôles internes 
 Agir comme expert de référence, notamment pour les CGI dans le cadre du programme d’attestation financière ;
 Évaluer la conception et l’efficacité des contrôles internes et recommander les améliorations requises ;
 Orienter la surveillance des CIIF, notamment les CGI fondée sur les risques afin d’assurer la fiabilité de l’information financière ;
 Analyser l’incidence des rapports SOC 1 et recommander les mesures appropriées ;
 Conseiller les responsables de contrôle et intervenir dans les dossiers complexes liés aux risques et aux programmes d’attestation.
 Influence et partenariat d’affaires 
 Exercer un leadership d’influence et conseiller les responsables de processus et contrôle et recommander les actions requises pour renforcer l’environnement de contrôle.
 Orientation du programme et évolution des pratiques 
 Contribuer à l’évolution des programmes de gouvernance financière en identifiant et en mettant en œuvre des améliorations fondées sur les risques, tout en anticipant les risques émergents et les impacts des technologies sur l’environnement de contrôle.

 Excellente compréhension des enjeux d’affaires et des risques organisationnels.
 Jugement stratégique permettant de naviguer dans des contextes complexes, ambigus ou sensibles.
 Leadership d’influence favorisant l’alignement et la mobilisation des parties prenantes.
 Grande capacité à simplifier des enjeux complexes et à communiquer efficacement avec les instances décisionnelles.
 Autonomie, rigueur et forte imputabilité quant à la qualité et à l’impact des recommandations.
 Habileté à piloter plusieurs dossiers stratégiques à la fois, tout en établissant les priorités et en coordonnant les contributions nécessaires.
 Ce que vous apportez 
 Titre professionnel CPA ;
 Minimum de huit (8) ans d’expérience pertinente en audit externe, audit interne ou gouvernance financière ;
 Excellentes connaissances des contrôles internes, du règlement 52-109 ou du Sarbanes-Oxley Act.
 Connaissances des contrôles généraux informatiques (CGI/ITGC) et des cadres de référence reconnus tels que COBIT, ainsi que des rapports d'assurance sur les contrôles des organismes de services (rapports SOC 1) et de leur incidence sur les CIIF.
 Connaissances approfondies des pratiques et concepts financiers, des processus liés au milieu de l'investissement (un atout).
 Expérience démontrée dans l’orientation, la conception et la mise en œuvre de méthodologies de contrôle interne, de cadres de gouvernance et de programmes de surveillance fondés sur les risques, ainsi que dans la défense de recommandations stratégiques auprès d’instances décisionnelles.
 Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais*, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.

 Sentir que mon rôle est important. Avoir du plaisir au quotidien. Pouvoir évoluer au rythme de mes ambitions. Obtenir une rémunération à la hauteur de ma contribution. C’est l’expérience professionnelle que m’offre La Caisse!

 La Caisse offre des chances d’emploi égales à tous et toutes. Elle invite les femmes, les membres des minorités visibles et ethniques, les personnes autochtones et les personnes handicapées à présenter leur candidature. Si cette offre d’emploi vous motive, mais que vous ne correspondez pas à tous les critères, contactez-nous quand même!
 La Caisse s’engage également à poursuivre la promotion de l’équité, de la diversité et de l’inclusion comme valeur clé et à en faire une source d’enrichissement et de fierté pour tous les membres de l’organisation. Veuillez nous informer si votre condition actuelle nécessite des mesures d’adaptation dans le cadre du processus de recrutement.
 La Caisse représente la Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec et ses filiales.

Who We Are   
 Rising Edge Group is an electrical contracting company founded in 2002, specialization in high-voltage electrical solutions that power critical infrastructure across North America. With operations in both Canada and the United States, we partner with clients across the electrical utilities, renewable energy, and industrial sectors to design, build, and maintain the critical infrastructure systems communities and industries rely on.

Guided by our STRIDE values - Safety, Teamwork, Responsibility, Integrity, Deliver, and Excellence - we foster a people focused on a culture of growth, mentorship and collaboration where safety always come first.

 Reporting to the Construction Manager, the Site Supervisor is responsible for managing and overseeing all daily on-site construction activities. This role leads site crews to ensure projects are executed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and within budget. The Site Supervisor serves as the primary point of contact for the Project Manager, subcontractors, and the client, and is accountable for timely and accurate crew timesheet submission.
 Key Responsibilities 
 The responsibilities include, but may not be limited to: 
 Oversee and coordinate all on-site construction activities to ensure compliance with project drawings, specifications, schedules, budgets, and quality standards 
 Lead, supervise, and support site crews, fostering productivity, accountability, and teamwork 
 Ensure daily completion and submission of crew timesheets 
 Act as the primary liaison between the company, client representatives, subcontractors, and on-site personnel

 Collaborate with the Project Manager to meet construction timelines through effective planning and use of manpower, materials, tools, and equipment 
 Monitor and maintain quality of workmanship in accordance with design documents and project requirements 
 Mentor, train, and motivate crew members to support continuous improvement and safe work practices 
 Coordinate with the Project Manager and client to review, track, and resolve RFIs (Requests for Information) and COs (Change Orders) 
 Support internal and external audits, inspections, and compliance activities
 Ensure all electrical work complies with Technical Safety BC requirements, applicable permits and inspections, and company standards
 Additional Information     
 This position supports projects throughout British Columbia and will require travel within the province.
 This position is designated as safety-sensitive making employment contingent upon the successful completion of pre-employment drug and alcohol testing, as well as criminal and general background checks. 
 Schedule & Compensation

 Standard workdays are 10 hours (7:00 a.m. – 5:30 p.m.)

 What We're Looking For   
 Degree in Construction Management or a related field, or a Journeyperson Electrician designation 
 Valid class 5 driver’s license or equivalent with an acceptable driving record 
 5–7 years of experience in the construction industry 
 Experience in BC Hydro or utility-related work preferred
 PSSP/WPP, CAT5, or equivalent utility safety training considered an asset
 High-voltage experience considered a strong asset
 Thorough knowledge of the Canadian Electrical Code (CEC) with BC Amendments, Technical Safety BC requirements, and WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety regulations as they relate to electrical and utility work
 Working knowledge of construction methods, safety regulations, scheduling, cost control, quality management, and interpretation of engineering drawings 
 Ability and willingness to work out of town 
 Able to travel including travelling to remote sites.
 Able to work in adverse weather conditions.
 Demonstrate problem solving and analytical skills with the ability to work within strict deadlines.
 Must show that you can work in a safe manner with respect to the environment, health and safety issues in the workplace.
 What We Offer 
 Competitive compensation with weekly pay periods 
 Overtime opportunities (project dependent)  
 Generous paid time off  
 RRSP-DPSP employer matching, increasing with years of service 
 Comprehensive benefits package (medical, dental, vision, and disability)  
 Company-paid safety training  
 Annual PPE allowance provided for field-based employees (post-probation)  
 Out-of-town work includes either all-inclusive camp accommodations or LOA and individual accommodations (project dependent) 
 Travel time to and from site will be paid at base rate, and travel provided by employer (project dependent)  
 Ongoing training, development, and career advancement opportunities 
 Employee Assistance Program (confidential counselling support) 
 Employee Referral Bonus Program  
 Why Rising Edge Group?

Our unwavering commitment to safety and quality drives excellence on every project, every day.   
 People-First Culture :  You’re more than a job title.  Every person contributes to powering essential energy infrastructure across North America. Our teams are built on collaboration, respect, and accountability. We support our employees through meaningful engagement initiatives, team events, and a culture that prioritizes wellbeing, inclusion, and genuine lasting connections.                                                                                                     
 Career Growth & Impact :  Your role is a path to a long-term career.  We empower our employees with hands-on experience, exposure to diverse projects, and opportunities to advance across disciplines, locations, and career paths. Through continuous learning, mentorship, and professional development, you’ll build lasting expertise while making a tangible impact in an environment where teamwork and integrity guide our work. 
 Reward & Recognition :  We believe skill, dedication, and excellence deserves recognition . Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a strong culture of appreciation ensure your achievements are celebrated, your growth is supported, and your work truly makes a difference.   
 At Rising Edge Group, you’re not just building projects, you’re building a meaningful career where your work helps power the future, one project at a time.

 Vision Loss Rehabilitation Canada (VLRC) is a national health services organization dedicated to empowering people who are blind or partially sighted to live safely and independently.  Position Title: Clinical Service Coordinator 
 Location: New Westminster, BC
 Status: Full-time, Contract – till March 17, 2028; existing vacancy
 Reports To: Manager, Healthcare Operations
 Compensation: $38 - $42/ hour
 Posting Date: September 3, 2026
 Closing Date: October 2, 2026
 Why Join VLRC? 
 This is an opportunity to play a pivotal role in an innovative Hospital-to-Home transition program that improves outcomes for individuals adjusting to vision loss. You will work alongside healthcare providers, rehabilitation specialists, and community partners to help clients regain independence, access critical supports, and successfully navigate life beyond hospital discharge. The role offers meaningful client impact, strong interdisciplinary collaboration, and the opportunity to help shape innovative approaches to integrated rehabilitation care.
 I. Position Summary 
 The Clinical Service Coordinator is responsible for supporting individuals experiencing vision loss as they transition from hospital to home and community-based rehabilitation services. Serving as the primary point of contact from referral through service delivery, this role provides case management, care coordination, system navigation, and client advocacy to ensure individuals receive timely access to rehabilitation, healthcare, and community supports.
 Working closely with hospitals, healthcare providers, clients, families, and VLRC's interdisciplinary team, the Clinical Service Coordinator helps remove barriers to care, supports successful transitions, and promotes client independence, safety, and quality of life. Success in this role requires strong case management, discharge and transition planning, care coordination, sound clinical judgment, exceptional relationship-building skills, and the ability to navigate complex healthcare and community service systems. Knowledge of vision rehabilitation is an asset; however, comprehensive training related to vision loss, rehabilitation pathways, and VLRC services will be provided.
 II. Key Responsibilities 
 Client Assessment, Case Management & Service Planning 
 ·         Serve as the primary point of contact for clients referred to the Hospital-to-Home Program, leading intake, needs assessment, service planning, and coordination of supports throughout the transition from hospital to community-based rehabilitation. 
 ·         Conduct intake, needs and risk assessments to identify client goals, rehabilitation priorities, support requirements, and barriers to independence and community living. 
 ·         Develop and monitor individualized service plans that connect clients with appropriate rehabilitation, healthcare, and community resources. 
 ·         Apply sound judgment to prioritize referrals, identify safety or psychosocial concerns, and facilitate timely intervention or referral when required. 
 ·         Establish baseline outcomes and monitor progress to support successful transitions and achievement of client goals.
 Care Coordination and Healthcare Transitions 
 ·         Coordinate admission to VLRC services and facilitate timely commencement of appropriate rehabilitation supports.
 ·         Collaborate with hospitals, healthcare providers, community organizations, and referral partners to develop integrated transition plans and support positive client outcomes. 
 ·         Assess discharge readiness, support systems, living circumstances, and service requirements to ensure continuity of care across providers and settings.
 ·         Serve as the central liaison among clients, families, healthcare professionals, and rehabilitation teams, facilitating communication, problem-solving, and shared care planning to rehabilitation, healthcare, and community supports.
 ·         Participate in case conferences, discharge-planning discussions, and interdisciplinary care meetings.
 ·         Support clients and families in navigating complex healthcare and community systems while advocating for access to appropriate services and resources.
 Documentation, Outcomes and Follow-Up 
 ·         Ensure accurate and timely documentation of client interactions, assessments, service plans, outcomes, and follow-up activities in compliance with organizational and professional standards. 
 ·         Monitor client progress, service delivery metrics, and rehabilitation outcomes to support informed decision-making and program effectiveness. 
 ·         Facilitate successful transitions of care by coordinating follow-up activities, resolving outstanding service needs, and supporting planned case closures
 Quality, Safety and Program Development 
 ·         Identify and escalate clinical, psychosocial, accessibility, and service-related risks in accordance with organizational standards.
 ·         Contribute to program evaluation, quality improvement, and outcome measurement initiatives that support evidence-informed practice and continuous service enhancement. 
 ·         Analyze emerging trends, service gaps, and system barriers to inform recommendations that improve client access, care coordination, and rehabilitation outcomes.
 ·         Foster collaborative partnerships through education, consultation, and outreach that increase awareness of vision rehabilitation services and strengthen integrated care pathways. 
 ·         Support the ongoing development and refinement of hospital-to-home programs, referral pathways, and service delivery models.
 ·         Other duties as required.
 III. What You’ll Bring to the Role 
 ·         Experience coordinating care and services for individuals with complex health, rehabilitation, or psychosocial needs. 
 ·         Advanced care coordination and case-management skills.
 ·         Strong assessment, problem-solving, and clinical judgment skills, with the ability to identify priorities, risks, and opportunities for intervention. 
 ·         Proven ability to manage multiple clients, competing priorities, and timelines in a fast-paced healthcare or community setting. 
 ·         Exceptional relationship-building and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across interdisciplinary teams and community partners. 
 ·         Knowledge of healthcare, rehabilitation, community support, and social service systems, with the ability to navigate services and advocate for client needs. 
 ·         Excellent communication, documentation, and organizational skills. 
 ·         A commitment to person-centered, culturally responsive, and accessible service delivery.
 Qualifications 
 ·         Degree in Social Work, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Nursing, Rehabilitation Sciences, Health Sciences, Disability Management, Healthcare Administration, or a related field. 
 ·         Minimum three years of experience in care coordination, hospital discharge planning, healthcare transitions, rehabilitation services, complex care, community health, or a related setting.
 ·         Experience working within interdisciplinary healthcare or community-based teams to support individuals with complex medical, functional, psychosocial, or accessibility needs.
 ·         Knowledge of vision rehabilitation and the impact of vision loss is considered an asset.
 Additional Requirements 
 ·         Registration in good standing with a relevant provincial regulatory body (e.g., Social Work, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Nursing) is considered an asset. 
 ·         Equivalent combinations of education and directly related experience will be considered. 
 ·         Valid driver's license and ability to travel as required.
 ·         Current satisfactory Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check
 At VLRC, your work has real impact. Join a team that empowers Canadians with vision loss to live independently, and where your growth, well-being, and contributions matter. We offer:
 ·         Comprehensive benefits, including health, vision, dental, corporate discounts, and an employee and family assistance program
 Flexible work arrangements, generous paid time off, and work-life balance initiatives
 Career development through training, mentorship, and advancement opportunities
 ·         Inclusive work culture with supportive teams, employee recognition, a joy-in-work wellness program, and mental health supports
 Join us to grow your career and make a difference every day.
 Inclusion, Accessibility & Accommodation 
 VLRC is committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive, equitable, and accessible workplace. We welcome applications from members of groups that have been historically marginalized, including but not limited to Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, including people who are blind, partially sighted, or deafblind, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ communities. Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 Superviser et gérer l’exécution des contrats (y compris les actions visant à corriger une performance non conforme) pour les sites fournisseurs sous ta responsabilité.

 DoorDash is building the future of local commerce through New Verticals, including grocery, convenience, retail, and other emerging categories. Our International New Verticals team supports the growth and development of these businesses across Canada, Australia, and New Zealand (“CANZ”).
 Our team partners across Operations, Product, and Finance to develop strategies that support sustainable growth across Canada.
 About the Role 
 We are hiring a data-driven and entrepreneurial Associate Manager, International New Verticals Strategy & Operations to lead strategy, experimentation, and go-to-market execution for fulfillment cost and profitability initiatives. 
 Your primary focus will be initiatives that improve costs and variable profit and the long-term economics of our New Verticals businesses. This may include dasher and operational efficiency, pricing accuracy, and other product or platform investments.
 You will own initiatives across the full product lifecycle: defining the problem, sizing the opportunity, developing and executing solutions, and measuring results after rollout.
 You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… 
 Develop strategy. Use insights, market context, data analysis, and financial modeling to identify and prioritize opportunities that improve the unit economics of our international New Verticals businesses.Lead experimentation. Design and execute pilots and experiments, partnering with Analytics, Product, Engineering, Finance and Accounting to develop robust cost / profitability problem statements, define success criteria, and translate findings into product and operations recommendations.Own end-to-end execution. Lead initiatives from initial planning through rollout, including defining the target audience, positioning, market readiness, operating changes, communications, training, dependencies, and launch timelinesAnalyze performance and influence decisions. Build SQL-based reporting and analytical frameworks to evaluate opportunities, measure performance, and inform investment and prioritization decisions.
 Lead, collaborate and Influence. Partner with and influence cross-functional teams including growth, quality, finance, product, analytics and engineering to launch initiatives to the finish line. 
 We’re excited about you because… 
 You have 4+ years of experience in product operations, product strategy, business operations, strategy and operations, consulting, or a related field.
 You have led complex, cross-functional initiatives in a fast-paced or high-growth environment.
 You can structure ambiguous problems, identify the most important questions, and translate them into clear plans, decisions, and deliverables.
 You are comfortable influencing Product, Engineering, Analytics, and business stakeholders without direct authority.
 You have experience designing experiments, evaluating results, and using insights to make strategic recommendations.
 You are analytically strong and comfortable working with large datasets, building financial models, and using SQL to answer business questions.
 You are an excellent written and verbal communicator who can distill complex product and technical concepts for different audiences.
 You are operationally rigorous and able to manage launch timelines, dependencies, risks, and market readiness across multiple workstreams.
 You hold a bachelor’s degree.
 Compensation 
 Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location. 
 In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.
 DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package for all regular employees, that includes paid time off, paid parental leave, wellness benefit and several paid holidays.
 Additionally, for full-time employees, DoorDash offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, disability and basic life insurance, an RRSP including an employer match, and a mental health program, among others.
 To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here .
 The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographical market up to our highest geographical market within British Columbia.
 $116,000 — $145,000 CAD 
 About DoorDash 
 At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.
 DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. 
 Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 
 We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

 We're looking for a Principal Software Developer to join the Elasticsearch - Search Infra team. This role provides technical vision and direction for Elasticsearch’s core search infrastructure, including indexing, retrieval, and relevance, and requires deep expertise in search internals and cross-team collaboration.

At our best, we write fast, scalable and intuitive software. We believe that the best way to do that is to empower individual engineers, code review every change, decide big things by consensus, and strive for incremental improvements.
 What You Will Be Doing: 
 As a full-time Elasticsearch contributor, you will define, lead, and contribute to the evolution of core search and indexing capabilities. You’ll research advances in search infrastructure, data structures, and retrieval algorithms to ensure we’re building the most efficient and powerful foundations for our users. You’ll work closely with our partners and product teams to understand their needs and help shape the long-term technical vision for search at Elastic. You’ll bring your past experience with large-scale search systems to drive an innovative roadmap for Elasticsearch’s indexing, query execution, and relevance layers.  Experience leading technical projects in the search infrastructure and distributed systems space. You bring proven knowledge in building and operating sophisticated search platforms and engineering robust, high-performance software systems.

 Experience with large-scale data or search systems such as Elasticsearch, Lucene, Solr, or distributed storage engines, and an understanding of how they work and why they work that way.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Collaborating across distributed teams is challenging, we value being supportive, empathetic, and trusting in all interactions, and we expect the same from everyone on the team.

 Maîtriser les bases de l’optimisation des effets visuels, incluant le nombre de particules, le surdébit, le coût des shaders, la mémoire des textures, les taux d’apparition, les paramètres d’évolutivité et les contraintes de performance de la plateforme.
 S’assurer que les effets sont lisibles, performants et alignés sur les besoins de jouabilité, la direction artistique, la dynamique, l’ambiance et les commentaires des joueurs.
 Passer en revue le travail des artistes internes, des studios partenaires ou des fournisseurs externes et fournir des commentaires clairs, constructifs et concrets.
 Aider à maintenir un seuil de qualité constant pour un ensemble d’effets, une fonctionnalité, un niveau ou une petite équipe.
 Soutenir la planification à court terme en aidant à décomposer les demandes d’effets visuels en tâches claires, priorités, dépendances, risques et critères de validation.
 Identifier de manière proactive les risques liés à la production, incluant les ancrages de jouabilité manquants, les pics de performance, une direction floue, les lacunes du processus, les problèmes de dépendance ou une exécution de styles incohérente.
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les concepteurs, les artistes conceptuels, les directeurs artistiques, les artistes techniques, les ingénieurs, les animateurs, les concepteurs audio et les producteurs.
 Contribuer à la communication avec les clients, selon les besoins, en clarifiant les exigences, en partageant les travaux en cours, en expliquant les contraintes et en s’alignant sur les résultats visés.
 Contribuer à l'amélioration des flux de travaux d’effets visuels, des modèles réutilisables, de la documentation, des bibliothèques, des normes de nomenclature ou des règles d’évolutivité, selon les besoins.
 Exigences
 Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle dans l’industrie des jeux vidéo en tant qu’artiste en effets visuels en temps réel ou dans un rôle similaire.
 Au moins un titre de jeu livré.
 Expérience éprouvée dans les flux des travaux en effets visuels en temps réel de bout en bout, depuis la conception et la création des ressources jusqu’à la mise en œuvre et le peaufinage dans le moteur.
 Solide expérience de la mise en œuvre d’effets dans Unreal Engine 4 ou 5, avec une excellente connaissance pratique de Niagara.
 Solides bases en animation de particules, incluant en matière de dynamisme, de rythme, de langage des formes, de mouvement, d’impact, d’anticipation, de dissipation et de lisibilité.
 Solide compréhension des énergies et des matériaux naturels tels que le feu, la fumée, l’eau, l’électricité, la magie, la poussière, les débris, les explosions, les phénomènes atmosphériques et les effets environnementaux.
 Solides compétences en création de matériaux et de textures avec des outils tels que Photoshop, Substance Designer ou des logiciels similaires.
 Capacité à créer des graphiques de matériaux et des systèmes d’effets visuels propres, lisibles et bien construits.
 Compréhension démontrée de l’optimisation des effets visuels en temps réel, incluant le nombre de particules, du surdébit, de l’utilisation de la mémoire, du coût des matériaux, de l’évolutivité et des contraintes de performance.
 Capacité à trouver un équilibre entre l’impact visuel, la clarté de la jouabilité, le coût technique et le calendrier de production.
 Excellentes compétences en communication, incluant dans la création de mises à jour écrites claires, de communications verbales, de documentation et de commentaires exploitables.
 Capacité à interpréter des directives créatives, de conception ou clients vagues et à les transformer en tâches d’effets visuels claires ou en plans de mise en œuvre.
 Expérience en mentorat, en analyse ou en soutien d’autres artistes. Un titre officiel de chef d’équipe n’est pas exigé, mais les comportements associés sont importants.
 Aisance à collaborer entre différentes disciplines et à travailler avec les équipes de conception, d’ingénierie, d’art technique, de production et de direction artistique.
 Grand sens des responsabilités, rigueur d’exécution, organisation et capacité à résoudre les problèmes.
 Intérêt pour évoluer vers des responsabilités de gestion plus larges avec le temps.
 Atouts
 Maîtrise des outils de production courants tels que Perforce, Jira, Miro et Confluence.
 Expérience avec Houdini.
 Expérience avec EmberGen.
 Expérience avec Unity.
 Expérience avec Substance Designer.
 Expérience avec des moteurs propriétaires ou des outils d’effets visuels personnalisés.
 Compétences en scriptage ou en programmation, comme C#, Python, Blueprint ou équivalent.
 Expérience en animation 2D ou en animation traditionnelle.
 Expérience en animation 3D, en simulation ou en création de contenu procédural.
 Expérience dans la création d’effets stylisés et réalistes.
 Expérience avec le feuillage, les atmosphères, les effets environnementaux, météorologiques, de destruction ou d’effets visuels d’ambiance.
 Expérience de travail avec des fournisseurs externes, des équipes de codéveloppements, des studios partenaires ou des fournisseurs externes.
 Expérience à collaborer avec des équipes issues de différents pays, cultures et fuseaux horaires.
 Expérience dans l’établissement de normes, de modèles, de conventions de nomenclature, de bibliothèques, de règles d’évolutivité ou de documentation de processus pour les effets visuels.
 Expérience pour soutenir les examens clients, les livraisons de jalons ou les boucles de rétroaction interstudios.
 Expérience dans la gestion de petites équipes, d’équipes d’intervention, de groupes de travail ou de groupes informels d’artistes.
 Exigences du portfolio
 Veuillez inclure un portfolio qui démontre clairement vos compétences en effets visuels en temps réel.
 Votre portfolio doit comprendre :
 Ressources d’effets visuels en temps réel avec une lisibilité, un minutage, un langage des formes et des éléments visuels facilement compréhensibles.
 Au moins un exemple dans un contexte de jeu en temps réel, de préférence, une vidéo montrant l’effet en jeu ou pendant une session de jeu interactive.
 Exemples de définition des matériaux et de travail de textures solides, avec des compositions nettes, lisibles et bien créées.
 Effets qui démontrent des bases telles que la composition, l’ambiance, le choix des couleurs, la dynamique, le mouvement, l’impact, la lisibilité et la compréhension des énergies naturelles.
 Exemples d’effets implémentés dans le moteur, de préférence dans Unreal Engine 4 ou 5, ou Niagara.
 Schémas détaillés montrant votre processus, incluant les textures, les matériaux, les émetteurs, la dynamique, l’implémentation, l’optimisation ou la configuration technique, le cas échéant.
 Explications claires de vos créations personnelles, en particulier pour tout travail réalisé en équipe.
 Les portefolios convaincants devraient inclure :
 Exemples avant/après montrant comment vous avez amélioré un effet grâce aux commentaires reçus, au mentorat, à l’optimisation ou à la direction artistique.

 Exemples de modèles, de bibliothèques, de systèmes de matériaux, de conventions de nomenclature, de configurations d’évolutivité ou d’améliorations de processus que vous avez aidé à créer.
 Exemples montrant comment vous avez équilibré la qualité visuelle et les contraintes de performance.

En plus de ses responsabilités en gestion de projet, il contribue activement à la conception et au développement des solutions techniques. Il agit comme principal point de contact auprès des clients, des sous-traitants et des équipes internes afin d’assurer l’exécution efficace des projets, de la définition des besoins jusqu’à la mise en service des équipements.
The Project Manager is responsible for the planning, coordination, and execution of custom automated and robotic equipment projects. The incumbent provides both technical and administrative leadership, ensuring compliance with customer requirements, budgets, schedules, and company quality standards.
In addition to project management responsibilities, the Project Manager actively contributes to the design and development of technical solutions. Acting as the primary point of contact for customers, subcontractors, and internal teams, the incumbent ensures the efficient execution of projects from requirements definition through equipment commissioning.

 Participer à l’analyse des besoins et des requis des clients. 
 Évaluer les projets, préparer les estimations de coûts et rédiger les propositions techniques et commerciales.

 Élaborer et maintenir les échéanciers de projet et assurer le suivi de leur avancement. 
 Assurer le contrôle et le suivi des budgets, des coûts et de la rentabilité des projets. 
 Préparer les ETC (estimations à compléter) et produire les rapports de suivi requis. 
 Organiser et animer les réunions de lancement, les rencontres de suivi client et les ateliers de travail. 
 Coordonner les activités des équipes internes et des fournisseurs impliqués dans les projets. 
 Assurer le suivi de la fabrication auprès des sous-traitants et veiller à la conformité des livrables. 
 Superviser les activités d’assemblage, d’intégration et d’essais des équipements. 
 Participer à la résolution des enjeux techniques et à l’amélioration continue des solutions développées. 
 Superviser les travaux effectués sur les sites des clients lors de l’installation des équipements.

 Assurer la satisfaction du client tout au long du cycle de vie du projet.

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Threat Operations is part of 1Password’s Security organization, bringing together Cyber Threat Intelligence, Detection Engineering, and Security Incident Response. Together we study how threat actors operate, turn that into high-quality detections, and respond quickly when something goes wrong. Interns work across all three teams, with time and focus shaped by your interests and our needs, so you see how intelligence becomes real defense. We care about turning intelligence into action, and we value blameless learning and psychological safety.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada/US. This position will be for 4 months - January to April 2027.



What You Can Expect:

 - Analyze incoming threat intelligence, assess its credibility and relevance to 1Password, and run IOC sweeps across our environment.

 - Own pieces of work across the threat management lifecycle, turning intel into recommendations for detection, incident response, and vulnerability management.

 - Join the alert triage rotation and learn how signal quality, enrichment, and response fit together.

 - Develop and test detection rules and response agents, and contribute to our detection-as-code and response-as-code platforms.

 - Build orchestration workflows to automate triage, enrichment, and response, using AI tools to help design and build them.



What we're looking for:

 - Confidence: A willingness to take on new challenges, and see them through to completion.

 - Humility: You're not afraid to ask "stupid" questions and make mistakes (as long as you learn from them).

 - Curiosity: You look for better ways of doing things, even if everyone seems happy with how they are.

 - Teamwork: We work together, and succeed as a team!



Bonus points for:

 - Familiarity with Git and managing infrastructure or detections as code, including Terraform.

 - Scripting or programming experience, such as Python or Go, and comfort working with APIs.

 - Exposure to SIEM and SOAR tools, logs, or writing detection rules and queries, through coursework, labs, or projects.

 - Experience using AI tools to build or automate workflows, with a healthy skepticism about their output.

 - Familiarity with frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK, plus security coursework, CTFs, home labs, or a security club.
   
   

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged at 1Password—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of most roles. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events. 


How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.


What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

🏝 Generous PTO policy - 2.08 days per month (1.5 work weeks per 4 month term)
💖 Company-wide wellness days (1 per quarter) 
🌎 Employee-led inclusion and belonging programs and ERGs
🏠 Remote-first environment
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
💡 1Password University access and learning sessions
🥳  Monthly internship events and socials

We believe in tech for good, and establishing Canada as a preferred destination for growing careers wherever we can!



You belong here.
